inlines.value: In this section, we’ll create a delimited sidebar block. The delimiter for the sidebar style is four asterisks (

Text in your document.

****
Enter the opening delimiter at the beginning of a new line and then press kbd:[Enter].

Text in your document.

****
This is content in a sidebar block.

image::name.png[]

This is more content in the sidebar block.
On the new line, enter your content, such as paragraphs, delimited blocks, directives, and macros. The delimited block’s style will be applied to all of this content until the closing delimiter.

Text in your document.

****
This is content in a sidebar block.

image::name.png[]

This is more content in the sidebar block.
****
To end the delimited block, press kbd:[Enter] at the end of your last line of content. On the new line, type the closing delimiter.
That’s it. You’ve built a delimited block.

In some cases, you can style a block using the style’s name. If the content is contiguous (not interrupted by empty lines or comment lines), you can assign the block style’s name in an attribute list placed above the content. This format is often used for single-line listings:

[listing]
sudo dnf install asciidoc
or single-line quotes:

[quote]
Never do today what you can put off `'til tomorrow.

However, note that the lines of a styled paragraph are first parsed like a paragraph, then promoted to the specified block type. That means that line comments will be dropped, which can impact verbatim blocks such as a listing block. Thus, the delimited block form is preferred, especially when creating a verbatim block.

paragraphs.value: Regular paragraph content (i.e., prose), offset on either side by an empty line. Must start flush to the left margin of the document. The block name can be used to convert the paragraph into most other blocks.
